items.actClause: AN ACT to authorize the creation of a state debt in the amount of three billion dollars, in relation to creating the "clean water bond act of 2017" to provide moneys for the preservation, enhancement, restoration and improvement of the quality of the state's water through the funding of certain projects and activities; and providing for the submission to the people of a proposition or question therefor to be voted upon at the general election to be held in November, two thousand seventeen
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3772

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to authorize the creation of a state debt in the amount of
three billion dollars, in relation to creating the "clean water bond
act of 2017" to provide moneys for the preservation, enhancement,
restoration and improvement of the quality of the state's water
through the funding of certain projects and activities; and providing
for the submission to the people of a proposition or question therefor
to be voted upon at the general election to be held in November, two
thousand seventeen

 PURPOSE :

To provide funds for enhancing the state's drinking water quality and
the preservation and restoration of the state's water resources.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one enacts the Clean Water Bond Act of 2017 which authorizes
the issuance of bonds in the amount of five billion dollars for
preserving, enhancing, restoring and improving the quality of the
state's water by the accomplishment of projects, including upgrades to
stormwater and wastewater infrastructure, and measures to enhance the
quality of the state's drinking water.

Section two provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Water quality and contamination is a serious and growing concern to
New Yorkers in all areas of the state. The contamination of drinking
water in several areas across the state has been a cause of great
concern and highlighted the need for increased focus, funding, and
resources dedicated solely to the quality of the state's water
supplies. Over this summer and fall the Senate and Assembly held a
series of hearings across the state to hear from officials, experts
and residents in order to gain an understanding of the water quality
issues they face. While the needs of the communities vary based on a
range of threats to their water, a consistent theme throughout these
hearings was the severe need for funding to support measures and
infrastructure upgrades these communities need. While there have been
state and federal funding sources established over the years, such as
the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (DWSRF), which offered low
interest loans and grants for water system improvement projects, and
the NYS Water Infrastructure Improvement Act of 2015, which provided
$200 million to municipalities for water quality improvement projects,
these programs have not been enough to meet the vast needs.  According
to a 2008 assessment by the Department of Health, the estimated cost
of repairing, replacing and updating New York's drinking water
infrastructure was $38.7 billion over the next 20 years plus an
additional $36.2 billion for municipal wastewater infrastructure. That
estimate is now almost a decade old and the needs have continued to
grow.

This legislation, as recommended in the Senate Standing Committees on
Health and Environmental Conservation's report Water Quality and
Contamination (see https://vtliumysenate.govlsitesidefaultifiles
/artieles/attachments/water quality _report.pdf), would provide much
needed funds to improve water infrastructure and quality without
forcing localities to rely on borrowing, thereby preventing any costs
from being passed on to residents. The Clean Water Bond Act provides
for flexibility to ensure funding is available to meet the varying
needs of communities. For example, in addition to infrastructure
needs, it could be used for the implementation of new filtration
systems, water quality related research and development, water
testing, and other measures for areas that suspect or know they have a
contamination issue and have not yet received Superfund status that
would make them eligible for other state funding.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

$5,000,000,000 state bond plus debt service.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Financial assistance to localities.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The act shall take effect immediately, provided that the provisions of
section one of this act shall not take effect unless and until the act
has been submitted to the people at the general election to be held in
November 2017, and shall have been approved by a majority of all votes
cast for and against it at such election. Upon approval by the people,
section one of this act shall take effect immediately.
